author: reek
body: `vec-extract` takes a `Vector 2`, so lanes 0 and 1 exist and lane 2 does not. The lane count is fixed by the builtin's own type, so this is decided at CHECK and the binary is never emitted.

author: reek
body: The negative half of the same guard is in codex/test/errors/vec-lane-negative.codex, and the two are separate files because they fail for different reasons: one compares against the lane count and one against zero. A single test naming CDX2093 would pass with half the check reverted.

author: reek
body: The positive control is codex/test/ops/vec-lanes-smoke.codex, which reads both legal lanes and a COMPUTED lane, and codex/test/vector-f32.codex, which reads lane 3 of a `Vector 4` through vec4-extract -- the last legal lane, which a check written with the wrong comparison would refuse.
